messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] CmdStan 2.1.0 is just about ready to go out.
parts:
There's no reason in principle to synchronize releases.
But I do think it's easier on our users that way, most of
whom are going to be using either RStan or PyStan.

So I'd like to keep our releases synched until it becomes
too much of a burden. Releasing CmdStan ahead of RStan/PyStan
just doesn't buy us much.

Anyone else have a preference?

The current plan is to break out CmdStan from Stan in the same
way as RStan or PyStan. Hopefully that'll be done by 2.2. Then
the drill will be to stabilize Stan, then update CmdStan,
RStan and PyStan. If we get more organized in the design of
Stan itself (also a target for 2.2), we can provide a reliable
warning of when the underlying Stan interface is stable so that
RStan/PyStan dev can work from there rather than waiting for
CmdStan/Stan to have ribbons on them.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] CmdStan 2.1.0 is just about ready to go out.
parts:
On 12/21/13, 2:53 PM, Ben Goodrich wrote:
> On Saturday, December 21, 2013 1:32:53 PM UTC-5, Bob Carpenter wrote:
>
> So I'd like to keep our releases synched until it becomes
> too much of a burden. Releasing CmdStan ahead of RStan/PyStan
> just doesn't buy us much.
>
> Anyone else have a preference?
>
>
> Anyone who wants to use CmdStan is more than capable of using git clone.

There's the overhead of installing git (it's not shipped with
either Mac OS or Windows), but GitHub also provides a zip download
button, so that's not really an issue.

I'm not sure, but I think you (Ben) are unusual in your willingness
to download and use pre-release software. I may be unusual
in the other direction, but I've never done it myself --- I
just wait for official releases. Partly that's because I hate
wrestling with software and learning new packages.

I do think our command-line users, especially the Linux users,
will be more tolerant of installation pain.

> So, I actually think releasing CmdStan ahead of
> the interfaces would be a negative.

Is the negative that it'll confuse/frustrate RStan and PyStan
users not to have the latest version?

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] CmdStan 2.1.0 is just about ready to go out.
parts:
On Saturday, December 21, 2013 3:30:51 PM UTC-5, Bob Carpenter wrote:
On 12/21/13, 2:53 PM, Ben Goodrich wrote:
> On Saturday, December 21, 2013 1:32:53 PM UTC-5, Bob Carpenter wrote:
>
>     So I'd like to keep our releases synched until it becomes
>     too much of a burden.  Releasing CmdStan ahead of RStan/PyStan
>     just doesn't buy us much.
>
>     Anyone else have a preference?
>
>
> Anyone who wants to use CmdStan is more than capable of using git clone.

There's the overhead of installing git (it's not shipped with
either Mac OS or Windows), but GitHub also provides a zip download
button, so that's not really an issue.
Either way, but I can't imagine why a CmdStan user would find installing git more costly than the time and bandwidth it takes to repeatedly download the whole thing as a .zip.

I'm not sure, but I think you (Ben) are unusual in your willingness
to download and use pre-release software.  I may be unusual
in the other direction, but I've never done it myself --- I
just wait for official releases.  Partly that's because I hate
wrestling with software and learning new packages.

There are a lot of people who only do official releases, but I think it is more a characteristic of binary / proprietary software. For open-source stuff, I think it is pretty normal for people to be downloading and building. I sometimes download and build the upstream source of something before it is officially released, but more often there is a Debian package with a pre-release of something. Often with R, I don't even realize I am using a pre-release until I see the startup banner.

Tracking origin/develop via git is a bit more ambitious than say downloading clang++ RC3. But under gitflow, the develop branch is always supposed to be useable, so I guess there are people that will use it.

In this case, I guess the best argument for releasing CmdStan ASAP is the wrong variance thing.

> So, I actually think releasing CmdStan ahead of
> the interfaces would be a negative.

Is the negative that it'll confuse/frustrate RStan and PyStan
users not to have the latest version?

That, but also having documentation on mc.stan.org that is out of sync with the Stan that RStan / PyStan is an interface to.

Ben

 

- Bob
